eligibility_text: Per state law and DVS regulation: veterans rated by the VA as 100% service-connected, permanent and total, who live in the home as their principal residence, and certain surviving spouses (veteran died on or after January 1, 2011, and the spouse has not remarried). Localities may not set income or asset limits or an application deadline. Call to confirm.
how_to_apply: File with the Commissioner of the Revenue (or other assessing official) in your city or county. Bring a VA summary of benefits letter showing the 100% permanent and total rating, the locality's affidavit or application form, and proof of residency such as a Virginia driver's license. Surviving spouses also need a death certificate and marriage certificate.
source_notes: Filing steps, documents and the no-deadline/no-income-limit rule from the DVS regulation 1VAC80-10-90 on law.lis.virginia.gov (loaded 2026-11-07). Eligibility, one-acre rule and surviving-spouse rules from Code of Virginia 58.1-3219.5 (loaded 2026-11-07). This is a benefit, not an office: no contact fields. A verifier could add the local Commissioner of the Revenue pages for Fredericksburg, Spotsylvania, Stafford, King George and Caroline. Cost type is unknown because the sources do not mention any filing fee. dvs.virginia.gov pages returned 403.

name: Real estate tax exemption for 100% disabled veterans and surviving spouses
organization: Virginia Department of Veterans Services and local Commissioners of the Revenue
description: Virginia law exempts the home of a veteran with a 100% service-connected, permanent and total VA disability rating from local real estate tax, along with up to one acre of land. A surviving spouse who does not remarry can keep the exemption.
source_name: Virginia Administrative Code, 1VAC80-10-90 (Department of Veterans Services)

eligibility_text: Per state law: the spouse, or a child age 16 to 29, of a service member killed, missing in action or taken prisoner during specified operations, or of a veteran the VA rates as "totally and permanently disabled or at least 90 percent permanently disabled," discharged under conditions other than dishonorable. Virginia residency rules apply, and the student must be admitted to a Virginia public college. Call to confirm.
how_to_apply: Call to ask how to apply. State law says the Commissioner of Veterans Services certifies eligibility, and the student must first be admitted to a Virginia public college or university.
source_notes: Description and eligibility from Code of Virginia 23.1-608 (loaded 2026-11-07). The statute does not describe the application steps or give contact details. The DVS VMSDEP page (dvs.virginia.gov) and the SCHEV military page returned 403, and the myvmsdep.dvs.virginia.gov portal did not resolve, so no phone, email or portal link is recorded. Search snippets mentioned a DVS VMSDEP phone and email, but those pages could not be loaded. The program changed in 2024 (tiers and stipends); a verifier should read the current DVS page. Stipends are covered in a separate section, 23.1-608.1, which was not read.
name: Virginia Military Survivors and Dependents Education Program (VMSDEP)
description: A state program that waives tuition and mandatory fees at Virginia public colleges and universities for spouses and children of certain veterans and service members who were killed, missing, captured or severely disabled.
